feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It reads professionally, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility.  
- Good use of scale and platform detail: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools make impact tangible.  
- Strong positioning for digital platform, governance, analytics, and multimedia leadership; the profile and skills align well with the experience.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Tighten bullets to emphasize outcomes over responsibilities. Several bullets start with “Led,” “Built,” or “Strengthened” but could show clearer business/user results.  
- Fix style inconsistencies and minor writing issues: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; maintain consistent punctuation in bullets; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” is stylistically inconsistent unless intentional branding.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector positioning. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so tightening it will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Replace “building the platforms” with a more active, outcome-oriented phrasing such as “leading digital platforms, governance, and content operations.”
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page websites” or “3.5M annual page views,” to increase specificity.
- Simplify the second sentence by grouping related areas: web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, and multimedia/AI experiences.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Drives enterprise website modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and multimedia programs, including AI-enabled search and user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search.”
- “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader” already conveys leadership, so avoid repeating too many broad leadership terms in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive leadership-level capabilities and used more parallel, concise phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use tighter, parallel noun phrases and remove filler words like “operations” where possible.
- Prioritize the strongest, most current differentiators: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream delivery
- If space is tight, swap “Multimedia production and livestream delivery” for a more strategic item such as “Cross-functional digital operations leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making it either more strategic or more tool-/domain-specific.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets and Topline Skills wording.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce the CV’s digital strategy range, but the block is too dense and repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add bullets and parallel structure: “Project name — outcome/what you built,” rather than paragraph-style entries.
- Tighten wording and remove filler: e.g., “AI-enabled legislative search combining hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Prioritize the most recent/high-value projects first and keep each to one line if space is tight.
- Standardize style and hyphenation: use “10 x 20-foot” (or “10-by-20-foot”) consistently; consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” and use one throughout.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance role and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” adds variety and is the least redundant; keep it if you need one distinctive project example.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground 3–4 highest-impact contributions, ideally with outcomes or scale.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and communications operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-oriented bullet: “Built cross-functional content workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make technical delivery more concise and outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, teams enabled, process time reduced, search success improved, or engagement/conversion gains from the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with the footer project list; avoid repeating named projects here unless you add outcomes.
- “Governance,” “workflows,” and “analytics” also echo prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this consulting engagement, especially AI-enabled search.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/enterprise scope, and what changed under your leadership rather than listing channels.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a high-volume public-sector organization.”
- Combine channel oversight bullets and add outcomes where possible: email engagement, social growth, video output, cost savings, faster publishing, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Rewrite website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia series.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with earlier NACo roles managing newsletters/video; keep this version at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video studio and advocacy content may duplicate Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same accomplishment verbatim.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and role level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and make outcomes explicit: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around launch/growth: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine planning/workflow bullets into one stronger line: “Built more structured editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent role bullets. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and operationally grounded.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise content governance for high-volume public-sector publishing.”
- Keep terminology aligned with recent experience: “cross-channel” may fit better than “multi-channel” given web, email, social, video, and AI search work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” closely repeat the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with project and work-experience language on storytelling, campaign platforms, and editorial coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is required for target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint and Power Pages” to reduce choppiness.
- If space allows, make impact more explicit: “Enterprise CMS modernization and technical execution” as the heading or first phrase.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation”; keep this section broader and less exhaustive.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating it verbatim multiple times.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio reporting; Microsoft Clarity behavioral analysis; KPI framework design; executive dashboarding; SEO and performance optimization”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Executive reporting” for clearer, more standard wording.
- Group tools by function to improve scanability and reduce list fatigue.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier such as “analytics infrastructure for enterprise web platforms” or “reporting for high-traffic digital properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; use this section for strategic analytics strengths and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and tied to recent in-house studio/event leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations
- Virtual event technical direction and show flow
- If accurate, add scale or scope language: “multi-camera,” “broadcast-quality,” “in-house studio,” or “recurring advocacy programming” to reflect recent leadership-level work.
- Keep this section skills-only; save outcomes like studio buildout or program expansion for Work Experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); consider shortening one of the two.
- Avoid repeating “hybrid/virtual event production” if similar language appears elsewhere in project or experience bullets.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. In this lower-priority technical section, make it more specific and current by signaling depth in the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider emphasizing level: **Drupal (advanced) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add brief qualifiers tied to recent work: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**
- If you want stronger differentiation from Topline Skills, rename the heading to **CMS Platforms** or **Content Platforms**
- Keep this item platform-only; avoid adding modernization or AI language here since those are already covered elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**
- “Drupal” is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects, so don’t over-explain it here

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, with clearer signal on modern tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied delivery, e.g. “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add specificity that reflects recent work: “custom Drupal front-end implementation,” “serverless scripting,” or “deployment automation.”
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: “JavaScript, API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, Google Tag Manager, HTML5, CSS3, jQuery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this version more technical/tool-specific.
- If GitHub Actions is the only CI/CD item, ensure it’s supported by work experience or recent projects.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped systems that signal use case: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp.”
- Move collaboration tools out of this line unless they are central to automation: Slack, Teams are better folded into a broader “Collaboration” item or removed for space.
- If accurate, add a short qualifier for impact: “Used to build editorial planning, approval workflows, cross-team intake, and reporting automations.”
- Consider tightening to the strongest, most recent tools only: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills.
- This item risks repeating Core Competencies without adding outcomes or specificity.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since email operations already appear in multiple NACo roles, this item should emphasize enterprise-grade systems and avoid restating newsletter work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/scale: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of only tool names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (campaign deployment)**
- If one platform was primary in the 2022–2024 director role, place it first and consider dropping the least relevant tool to keep the section tighter.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email/newsletter references in Work Experience; keep this item tool-focused rather than describing campaign execution.
- “Engagement” may also overlap with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations”; platform specificity helps reduce that.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is mostly a keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analytics infrastructure and optimization methods rather than repeating generic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI design” or “executive reporting” to sound more outcome-oriented and less generic.
- Replace “A/B testing” unless you can support it with a concrete example in recent roles; otherwise it may invite questions.
- Add Google Search Console if used, since it strengthens the SEO/measurement story more than the broad term “SEO.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this section more tool-specific while leaving concepts in Topline Skills.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating too many generic descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, since leadership, governance, and weekly video work are already covered in newer entries.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, livestream and video production operations.”
- Add concrete scope/results if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams/videos produced, email volume, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital production workflows.”
- If accurate, replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a clearer management phrase like “mentored a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; avoid repeating that phrase unless you distinguish this as the launch/origin stage.
- “strengthening workflows” is also echoed in later NACo entries; specify what changed or cut it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and undersells the standout achievement. Since later NACo roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize the podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest impact: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; partnered on digital and multimedia content to translate research into member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and tighten wording: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Remove vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” unless you can specify formats or outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating general multimedia/digital production language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; save management/operations emphasis for 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a cleaner tools list: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want to keep capabilities here, separate them clearly: “Tools: Adobe Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator | Production: livestream studio operations, podcast production”
- Use consistent naming style (“Adobe Premiere Pro,” not just “Premiere Pro”) for polish and ATS clarity.
